details.purpose: *To record details about a single, clinically significant finding identified on radiological examination that cannot be otherwise recorded using the CLUSTER.imaging_exam family of archetypes. (en)
details.keywords: *finding, imaging, body, system, observation, diagnostic, radiology, image (en)
details.use:
*Use to record details about a single, clinically significant finding identified on radiological examination that cannot be otherwise recorded using the CLUSTER.imaging_exam family of archetypes.
In practice, the design intent is for the CLUSTER.imaging_exam family of archetypes to be used to record all detailed findings on radiological examination. The family of specialised archetypes, derived from the generic parent archetype, are intentionally designed to be inclusive of all reasonably anticipated and relevant findings for each structure or region.
In situations where it is not possible to use one of the CLUSTER.imaging_exam family of archetypes, use this alternative CLUSTER.imaging_finding archetype to capture simple details about a single finding. In this way it is possible to record findings that are not yet available in an incomplete specialisation or to capture information about unanticipated or unexpected findings.
This archetype has been designed to be nested within the 'Structured imaging findings' SLOT in the OBSERVATION.imaging_exam_result or in 'Additional details' SLOT within a relevant CLUSTER.imaging_exam specialisation, but can also be used within other ENTRY or CLUSTER archetypes, where clinically appropriate. (en)
details.misuse: *Not to be used to record clinical findings that are already modelled within one of the CLUSTER.imaging_exam family of archetypes. (en)

items.items: Details about a single finding identified on radiological examination.
The presence or absence of a clinically significant finding.
Additional narrative about the imaging finding, not captured in other fields.
Additional structured details about imaging finding.
Identification of a significant clinical finding, by name.
Coding of 'Finding' with a terminology, such as SNOMED CT, is recommended. For example: free fluid; or abscess.
Narrative description about the clinically significant finding.
Simple description of anatomical location of the finding.
For example: Recto-uterine pouch. Coding of 'Body site' with a terminology, such as SNOMED CT, is desirable.
Structured details about the area of the body under examination.

For example: details about a relative anatomical location, such as '2cm distal to the appendix'. If the body site has been fully identified in the 'Body site' data element, then this SLOT becomes redundant.
It is not possible to determine if the finding is present or absent.
